---
title: "Gaussian elimination"
toc: true
---

Solve these three systems by **forward elimination**, followed by **back
substitution**. The last system needs a row swap before elimination can begin.

For an augmented matrix $[A\mid b]$, the last column contains the right-hand
side. Apply every row operation to that column too. A **pivot** is the nonzero
entry used to eliminate entries below it. If the proposed pivot is zero,
look for a nonzero entry below it and swap rows.

Work on paper first, then check your entries. Use exact numbers such as `1/2`.
The matrix fields below include the right-hand side as their last column.
Follow the specified row operations without further row scaling: other valid
elimination routes can produce different intermediate matrices.

## 1. A 2×2 system

$$
\begin{aligned}
x+y&=5,\\
2x-y&=1.
\end{aligned}
\qquad
[A\mid b]=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&5\\2&-1&1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

### A. Eliminate below the first pivot

Apply $R_2\leftarrow R_2-2R_1$, keeping $R_1$ unchanged.
Enter the resulting augmented matrix.

```{math-exercise}
#| label: gauss-2x2-elimination
#| caption: 1A — one elimination step
#| mode: equivalent
#| partial-credit: true

$[U\mid c]=$ mat[1,1,5;0,-3,-9]
```

### B. Back substitute

Use the second row to find $y$, then use the first row to find $x$.

```{math-exercise}
#| label: gauss-2x2-solution
#| caption: 1B — solve the triangular system
#| mode: equivalent
#| partial-credit: true
#| field-labels: x, y

$x=$ __[2]

$y=$ __[3]
```

<details class="learning-hint">
<summary>Hint for problem 1</summary>

In the second row, the coefficient of $y$ becomes $-1-2\cdot1$.
The right-hand side becomes $1-2\cdot5$. A row operation changes the whole row.
Check your final solution in both original equations.

</details>

## 2. A 3×3 system

$$
\begin{aligned}
x+y+z&=6,\\
2x+3y+z&=11,\\
x-y+2z&=5.
\end{aligned}
\qquad
[A\mid b]=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1&6\\2&3&1&11\\1&-1&2&5\end{bmatrix}.
$$

### A. Clear the first column

Use the unchanged first row in both operations:

$$R_2\leftarrow R_2-2R_1,\qquad R_3\leftarrow R_3-R_1.$$

```{math-exercise}
#| label: gauss-3x3-first-column
#| caption: 2A — eliminate x from rows 2 and 3
#| mode: equivalent
#| partial-credit: true

Resulting augmented matrix $=$ mat[1,1,1,6;0,1,-1,-1;0,-2,1,-1]
```

### B. Clear the second column

Using the **updated** rows from part A, apply
$R_3\leftarrow R_3+2R_2$. Keep the other rows unchanged.

```{math-exercise}
#| label: gauss-3x3-triangular
#| caption: 2B — complete forward elimination
#| mode: equivalent
#| partial-credit: true

$[U\mid c]=$ mat[1,1,1,6;0,1,-1,-1;0,0,-1,-3]
```

### C. Back substitute

Solve from the bottom row upward: first $z$, then $y$, then $x$.

```{math-exercise}
#| label: gauss-3x3-solution
#| caption: 2C — back substitution
#| mode: equivalent
#| partial-credit: true
#| field-labels: x, y, z

$x=$ __[1]

$y=$ __[2]

$z=$ __[3]
```

<details class="learning-hint">
<summary>Hint for problem 2</summary>

After part A, the first column below the pivot should contain only zeros.
The second pivot is 1. Adding twice the new second row to the new third row
eliminates its $y$ coefficient. The last row then contains only $z$ and the
right-hand side. Substitute your solution into all three original equations.

</details>

## 3. A 3×3 system that needs pivoting

$$
\begin{aligned}
2y+z&=1,\\
2x+y-z&=0,\\
x-y+2z&=9.
\end{aligned}
\qquad
[A\mid b]=\begin{bmatrix}0&2&1&1\\2&1&-1&0\\1&-1&2&9\end{bmatrix}.
$$

The first proposed pivot is zero, so division by it is impossible.
This does **not** mean the system has no unique solution.
Use **partial pivoting**: in the current column, choose the available entry
with the largest absolute value and move its row into the pivot position.
Here, compare the entries $0$, $2$, and $1$ in the first column.

### A. Choose and swap the pivot row

Enter the original row number to swap with row 1, then the augmented matrix
immediately after that swap. Do not eliminate or scale any rows yet.

```{math-exercise}
#| label: gauss-pivot-swap
#| caption: 3A — choose the first pivot
#| mode: equivalent
#| partial-credit: true

Swap row 1 with row __[2].

Matrix after the swap $=$ mat[2,1,-1,0;0,2,1,1;1,-1,2,9]
```

### B. Eliminate below the pivots

After the swap, the second row already has a zero in the first column.
Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-\tfrac12R_1$.

```{math-exercise}
#| label: gauss-pivot-first-column
#| caption: 3B — eliminate below the new first pivot
#| mode: equivalent
#| partial-credit: true

Resulting augmented matrix $=$ mat[2,1,-1,0;0,2,1,1;0,-3/2,5/2,9]
```

The second pivot is 2; the remaining entry below it is $-3/2$.
Since $|2|>|-3/2|$, partial pivoting requires no further swap.
Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3+\tfrac34R_2$ to the updated matrix.

```{math-exercise}
#| label: gauss-pivot-triangular
#| caption: 3B — complete forward elimination
#| mode: equivalent
#| partial-credit: true

$[U\mid c]=$ mat[2,1,-1,0;0,2,1,1;0,0,13/4,39/4]
```

### C. Back substitute

Solve for $z$, then $y$, then $x$. Row swaps change the order of the equations,
**not** the order of the unknowns: the columns still represent $x,y,z$.

```{math-exercise}
#| label: gauss-pivot-solution
#| caption: 3C — solve after pivoting
#| mode: equivalent
#| partial-credit: true
#| field-labels: x, y, z

$x=$ __[2]

$y=$ __[-1]

$z=$ __[3]
```

<details class="learning-hint">
<summary>Hint for problem 3</summary>

Swap the **entire** rows, including their right-hand sides. After the swap,
the first pivot is 2, so subtract half of row 1 from row 3.
For the next step, check that $-3/2+(3/4)\cdot2=0$.
Fractions during elimination are normal. Check your final answer in the
original system, before any row swaps.

</details>
